types.embedding_query_text: Vaccine: A substance used to stimulate the production of antibodies and provide immunity against one or several diseases. Also called immunization, inoculation, injection. Examples: Covid-19 vaccines, Covid-19 vaccine, Covid vaccine.

chosen_type.label: Drug
chosen_type.justification: Best match for vaccine as a medical substance

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: DoseSchedule
candidates.comment: A DoseSchedule is a MedicalIntangible specifying a particular regimen for administering a drug or supplement. Also called dosing regimen, medication schedule, treatment plan. Examples: "Take one pill daily", "Apply twice a day for 7 days", "Administer 500mg every 8 hours".

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

types.embedding_query_text: Politician: A person who is involved in politics, especially one who holds or seeks public office. Also called statesman, stateswoman, legislator. Examples: Ron Johnson, Rand Paul, Ted Cruz, Sen. Ron Johnson.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Politician is a person involved in politics

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: LegislativeBuilding
candidates.comment: A LegislativeBuilding is a government building civic structure where legislative bodies meet and conduct their work. Also called capitol building, parliament house, assembly hall. Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthOfficial: A person who holds a position of authority in a healthcare organization or government agency. Also called health administrator, medical director, public health official. Examples: Dr. Anthony Fauci, Fauci.

chosen_type.label: HealthOfficial
chosen_type.definition: A person who holds a position of authority in a healthcare organization or government agency
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in schema.org for a health official

candidates.label: PhysiciansOffice
candidates.comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. Distinct from Hospital, which offers inpatient care and emergency services.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalProfessional: A person who is trained and licensed to provide medical care and treatment to patients. Also called doctor, physician, healthcare provider. Examples: Dr. Kevin Ault, Dr. Brenna Hughes, Ault, Hughes.

chosen_type.label: Physician
chosen_type.justification: Medical professional often refers to a physician or doctor

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure specifically intended to treat a health condition or improve a patient's well-being. Also called medical treatment, therapy, healing procedure. Examples: chemotherapy, physical therapy, surgical removal of a tumor.

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing a process of care, invasive or non-invasive, used for diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, or palliative purposes. Also called medical intervention, clinical procedure, healthcare process. Examples: "surgery", "biopsy", "vaccination", "physical therapy".

candidates.label: Physician
candidates.comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.

candidates.label: MedicalTherapy
candidates.comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.

candidates.label: PhysiciansOffice
candidates.comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. Distinct from Hospital, which offers inpatient care and emergency services.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Journalist is a person, but there isn't a more specific type in schema.org

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: AskPublicNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Also called public appeal article, crowdsourced news request, call for information. Examples: a newspaper asking readers for stories about a local event, a news site requesting photos from a natural disaster, a journalist seeking expert opinions on a topic.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalOrganization: An organization that provides medical care, research, or education. Also called hospital, clinic, research institute. Examples: National Foundation for Infectious Diseases, Mayo Clinic, Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, NFID.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Direct match for an organization providing medical care

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

types.embedding_query_text: MedicalJournal: A publication that contains articles and research papers on medical topics. Also called journal, periodical, publication. Examples: New England Journal of Medicine, NEJM.

chosen_type.label: ScholarlyArticle
chosen_type.justification: Medical journal articles are a type of scholarly article

candidates.label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication. Examples: a peer-reviewed article on a new drug, a research paper on surgical techniques, a review article on a disease. Distinct from ScholarlyArticle, which is a broader category for academic papers.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: MedicalWebPage
candidates.comment: A web page that specifically provides medical information. Also called health information page, clinical webpage, medical content page. Examples: a page describing a disease, a page explaining a medical procedure, a doctor's profile page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a broader category for any web document.

candidates.label: PublicationVolume
candidates.comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

types.embedding_query_text: HealthOrganization: An organization that provides health-related services, research, or education. Also called health department, public health agency, non-profit organization. Examples: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, CDC.

chosen_type.label: MedicalOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Health organization is similar to medical organization

candidates.label: SportsOrganization

Examples: the U.S. Capitol, a state capitol building, the Houses of Parliament. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

chosen_type.label: OnlinePlatform
chosen_type.justification: Not a perfect match, but closest in schema.org for online platforms

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: BlogPosting
candidates.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: OnlineMarketplace
candidates.comment: An OnlineMarketplace, as an OnlineStore, is an e-commerce platform where multiple sellers offer products or services. Also called e-marketplace, digital marketplace, online bazaar. Examples: Amazon, eBay, Etsy. Distinct from OnlineStore, which is a single seller's e-commerce site.

chosen_type.label: Pandemic
chosen_type.definition: A widespread outbreak of a disease
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in schema.org for pandemic as an event

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: CDCPMDRecord
candidates.comment: A CDCPMDRecord is a StructuredValue representing a record in the CDC tabular data format used for hospital data reporting, specifically for COVID-19 related data. Also called CDC hospital data record, COVID-19 data record. Examples: a daily hospital bed occupancy report, a weekly ICU patient count record.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType

Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.
